Documentation → Automation & Change Control → Change requests

Change requests

A change request is the approval record for a risky, windowed change — which appliances, which services, when, how to roll back and who said yes — and the gate that lets the scheduler run it only inside an approved maintenance window.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereAutomation → Change Requests (URL /web/change-requests/); Administrator → Change Types (URL /administration/change-types/)

What is it?#

A change request (CR) records a planned change to one or more appliances: the type of change, the affected devices and the published services they take offline, the maintenance window, the risk, the rollback plan and the approval. It carries a permanent reference of the form CR-2026-0042.

A CR is also a gate. Destructive automations — firmware upgrade, reboot, HA failover, the Cert Manager lifecycle sweep, Custom REST call — run only when bound to an approved CR that covers them (same action, only the devices it names), and only while the clock is inside its window. For how this applies to each appliance and to the manual Upgrade page, see Putting an appliance under change control.

NAF block: Orchestrator. A change request coordinates the other blocks — an approval, a maintenance window in NetBox, the write action, the closing notice — and never touches an appliance itself; see Where SATOM sits in the NAF Framework.

What does it do?#

  • Guides you through raising a change: document language, change type, risk, proposed wording (filled in for you), devices and window.
  • Freezes the affected-service inventory at creation, so the record you approve is the record that runs.
  • Drives the lifecycle draft → approved → scheduled → in progress → completed / failed, or cancelled at any open stage, with every step on a Timeline. A closed change (completed, failed or cancelled) cannot be approved or cancelled again.
  • Binds a one-shot scheduled action at the window start.
  • Prints a formal change document and exports the affected services.
  • Sends a maintenance notice and, at the end, an outcome notice.
  • Optionally opens a ticket in Jira / OpenProject / Vikunja, queues your own integration hooks and opens a NetBox maintenance window (Integrations).
  1. 1DraftRaise the change: type, devices, window, wording. Inventory is frozen
  2. 2ApproveAn administrator approves; change.approved hooks fire
  3. 3ScheduleA one-shot action is bound at the window start
  4. 4In progressThe scheduler re-checks approval and window, then runs it
  5. 5Completed / failedClosed from the real outcome; outcome notice mailed

Requirements#

  • At least one registered appliance of a product the change type supports.
  • A window start before the change can be scheduled; the change can only run between window start and window end.
  • For e-mail notices: Settings → Email configured.
  • For tickets, hooks and NetBox: the matching card in Integrations.

Permissions#

Every Change Requests and Change Types page and action requires users.manage (Administrator). Without it the sidebar entries are hidden and the URLs answer 403. When a change is shown inside the Upgrade Flow to a user without that permission, the action bar reads "Read-only: driving this change needs the user-manage permission."

Change requests are scoped by the devices they name: a CR is visible in every ADOM that can see at least one of its devices. A CR naming no device is visible everywhere. A CR outside your ADOM answers 404.

ℹ️Note — Not the same as template approval

operations.template_approve approves configuration templates and provisioning items. It does not approve change requests.

How to use#

Raise a change request#

  1. Open Automation → Change Requests and press New Change Request. (A change can also be raised from an appliance's Upgrade Preparation with Raise change request, from the Upgrade Flow, from the HA failover page, or from a day on the Calendar.)
  2. 1 · Document language — the language the change document and the proposed text are drafted in. Pre-selected from your profile when set.
  3. 2 · Type of change — pick the Change type (nothing is pre-selected) and the Risk (Low, Medium, High; default Medium). Types marked documentary have no automation: "This change type has no automation behind it: the change request is raised, approved and printed here, and the work is carried out by hand. It cannot be bound to the scheduler."
  4. Scope & window — select the Affected devices (each labelled with its product) and the Window start / Window end. Both times are read in the timezone shown in the label (Settings → General) and stored as UTC.
  5. 3 · Proposed wording — Title, Reason and Rollback plan are filled in from the type, the devices and any cited pre-upgrade run, and stop updating as soon as you edit them (Restore proposal brings them back). Also set Change owner (Verantwortlicher), Notify on completion and Approval (Manual — approved here in SATOM or External — an integration must approve it).
  6. Press Create draft. Tick <strong>Export columns</strong> and press <strong>Download .xlsx</strong> or <strong>.csv</strong>.</li> <li><strong>External change record</strong> — approval mode, change ticket, NetBox window and the integration log.</li> <li><strong>Timeline</strong> — every event, who and when.</li> <li><strong>Maintenance notice</strong> — the client-facing notice text.</li> </ul> <h3 id="change-types-administrator-change-types">Change Types (Administrator → Change Types)<a class="dc-anchor" href="#change-types-administrator-change-types" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p>This page controls what the <strong>Change type</strong> picker offers and the text each type proposes and prints.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Built-in types</strong> come from the automation catalog (every action that touches a device and is destructive or changes objects). They raise, approve and print a change request, but cannot be scheduled.</li> <li>Text can be machine-translated into the other supported languages and each translation marked as reviewed.</li> <li>Deleting a built-in type's overrides resets it to the shipped wording.</li> </ul> <h2 id="configuration">Configuration<a class="dc-anchor" href="#configuration" title="Permanent link">#</a></h2> <div class="dc-table"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Field</th> <th>Description</th> <th>Required</th> <th>Example</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Document language</td> <td>Language of the change document and proposed text</td> <td>Yes</td> <td>English</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Change type</td> <td>A change-controlled action or a documentary type</td> <td>Yes</td> <td><em>Reboot the appliance (DESTRUCTIVE)</em></td> </tr> <tr> <td>Risk</td> <td><code>low</code>, <code>medium</code>, <code>high</code></td> <td>No (default medium)</td> <td>high</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Title</td> <td>Short name of the change</td> <td>Yes</td> <td><em>Reboot fweb-01 after kernel patch</em></td> </tr> <tr> <td>Reason</td> <td>Printed next to the standard justification</td> <td>No</td> <td>—</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Rollback plan</td> <td>What undoes the change, from what backup</td> <td>No</td> <td>—</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Change owner (Verantwortlicher)</td> <td>Printed in §1; A scheduled run touches only these devices</td> <td>Required to schedule</td> <td><code>fweb-01</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>Window start / Window end</td> <td>In the console timezone; end must be after start</td> <td>Start required to schedule</td> <td><code>2026-11-07 22:00</code></td> </tr> </tbody> </table></div> <h2 id="example">Example<a class="dc-anchor" href="#example" title="Permanent link">#</a></h2> <div class="dc-co dc-co-example"> <p class="dc-co-title"><span class="dc-co-ico">🧪</span>Example — Reboot one FortiWeb on Saturday night</p> <p>Raise a change: language English, type <strong>Reboot the appliance (DESTRUCTIVE)</strong>, risk High, device <code>fweb-01</code>, window 22:00–23:00. <strong>Create draft</strong>, review the change document, <strong>Approve</strong>, then <strong>Schedule</strong>. The bound one-shot action <code>CR #12: Reboot fweb-01</code> fires at 22:00; the change moves to <em>in progress</em>, the reboot is sent, and the change closes as <em>completed</em> with the summary <em>"fweb-01: reboot accepted (HTTP 200) …"</em>. The outcome notice is mailed to the notify list.</p> </div> <h2 id="result">Result<a class="dc-anchor" href="#result" title="Permanent link">#</a></h2> <ul> <li>Status moves along the lifecycle; each transition adds a timeline event (<code>draft</code>, <code>approved</code>, <code>scheduled</code>, <code>in_progress</code>, <code>completed</code>, <code>failed</code>, <code>cancelled</code>, plus <code>edited</code>, <code>rollout_planned</code>, <code>crq_requested</code>, <code>window_opened</code>, <code>notified</code>, <code>device_result</code>…).</li> <li>A fire that is refused by the gate (not approved, outside the window, waiting for external approval) leaves the change <strong>untouched</strong>; the run is recorded as <em>skipped</em>. A fire that does run closes the change: <code>ok</code> → <strong>completed</strong>, anything else → <strong>failed</strong>. A live run from an appliance page records that appliance's result on the timeline and closes the change only when every appliance it names has a result (see <a href="change-control.html">Change control</a>).</li> <li>On closing: the NetBox window (if any) is closed, <code>upgrade.finished</code> / <code>upgrade.failed</code> hooks fire per device, and the outcome notice — <em>Maintenance completed - service restored</em> or <em>Maintenance window closed - change NOT completed</em> — is mailed once.</li> <li>Audit entries: <code>change_request.create</code>, <code>.update</code>, <code>.approve</code>, <code>.schedule</code>, <code>.cancel</code>, <code>.closed_by_hand</code>, <code>.external_approval</code>, <code>.notified</code>, <code>.crq_requested</code>, <code>.crq_recorded</code>, <code>.window_opened</code>, <code>.document</code>; an external approval sent through the API is logged as <code>api.change_request.external_approval</code> (refusals as <code>api.change_request.external_approval_refused</code>).</li> </ul> <h2 id="troubleshooting">Troubleshooting<a class="dc-anchor" href="#troubleshooting" title="Permanent link">#</a></h2> <h3 id="does-not-run-against-it-supports">"<type> does not run against <product> (<devices>). It supports: …"<a class="dc-anchor" href="#does-not-run-against-it-supports" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Possible causes</strong> — a selected device's product is not supported by the chosen change type.</p> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — deselect the named devices or choose another type. Nothing was created.</p> <h3 id="the-maintenance-window-ends-at-or-before-it-starts-so-no-instant-lies-inside-it-and-the-change-could-never-fire">"The maintenance window ends at or before it starts, so no instant lies inside it and the change could never fire."<a class="dc-anchor" href="#the-maintenance-window-ends-at-or-before-it-starts-so-no-instant-lies-inside-it-and-the-change-could-never-fire" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — correct the window; the end must be later than the start.</p> <h3 id="approve-the-change-request-before-scheduling-it-set-a-maintenance-window-start-first">"approve the change request before scheduling it" / "set a maintenance-window start first"<a class="dc-anchor" href="#approve-the-change-request-before-scheduling-it-set-a-maintenance-window-start-first" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — approve the change, or <strong>Edit</strong> it and set a window start, then press <strong>Schedule</strong> again.</p> <h3 id="name-at-least-one-appliance-before-scheduling-an-automated-change-runs-only-against-the-devices-it-names">"name at least one appliance before scheduling: an automated change runs only against the devices it names"<a class="dc-anchor" href="#name-at-least-one-appliance-before-scheduling-an-automated-change-runs-only-against-the-devices-it-names" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Possible causes</strong> — you pressed <strong>Schedule</strong> on a change that names no appliance. Such a change can be saved and read, but not scheduled.</p> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — <strong>Edit</strong> the change and select its affected devices, approve it again if needed, and press <strong>Schedule</strong> again.</p> <h3 id="change-request-n-authorizes-x-not-y-change-request-n-does-not-cover-device-ids-change-request-n-authorizes-named-devices-this-action-targets-the-whole-fleet">"change request #N authorizes 'X', not 'Y'" / "change request #N does not cover device id(s) …" / "change request #N authorizes named devices; this action targets the whole fleet"<a class="dc-anchor" href="#change-request-n-authorizes-x-not-y-change-request-n-does-not-cover-device-ids-change-request-n-authorizes-named-devices-this-action-targets-the-whole-fleet" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Possible causes</strong> — a scheduled action bound to this change is for another action, targets a device the change does not name, or targets the whole fleet while the change names devices. The run is recorded as <em>skipped</em> and the change is left untouched.</p> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — run the work through a change that names that action and those devices, and let its <strong>Schedule</strong> button create the bound action.</p> <h3 id="is-a-documentary-change-type-it-has-no-automated-executor">"'<type>' is a documentary change type: it has no automated executor. …"<a class="dc-anchor" href="#is-a-documentary-change-type-it-has-no-automated-executor" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Possible causes</strong> — you tried to schedule a type created under Change Types.</p> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — carry the work out by hand during the window, then press <strong>Mark completed</strong> or <strong>Mark failed</strong> on the change to close it.</p> <h3 id="the-bound-action-ran-but-was-skipped-with-change-request-before-the-maintenance-window">The bound action ran but was "skipped" with "change request: before the maintenance window"<a class="dc-anchor" href="#the-bound-action-ran-but-was-skipped-with-change-request-before-the-maintenance-window" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Possible causes</strong> — the window moved after scheduling, or the action fired outside it. The change is not touched by a refused fire.</p> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — <strong>Edit</strong> the window if needed (this voids the approval), approve again and <strong>Re-schedule</strong>.</p> <h3 id="this-changes-maintenance-window-closed-at-so-there-is-no-time-left-to-run-it">"This change's maintenance window closed at …, so there is no time left to run it."<a class="dc-anchor" href="#this-changes-maintenance-window-closed-at-so-there-is-no-time-left-to-run-it" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Possible causes</strong> — <strong>Schedule</strong> was pressed after the window end. (Pressed while the window is open, the run is set to start one minute from now.)</p> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — <strong>Edit</strong> the change to a future window (this voids the approval), approve it and <strong>Schedule</strong> again.</p> <h3 id="the-change-stays-in-progress-after-its-window-ended">The change stays "in progress" after its window ended<a class="dc-anchor" href="#the-change-stays-in-progress-after-its-window-ended" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Possible causes</strong> — a live run did not cover every appliance the change names, so not every appliance has a result.</p> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — press <strong>Mark completed</strong> or <strong>Mark failed</strong> on the change.</p> <p><strong>Verification</strong> — the change shows the chosen status and the outcome notice is mailed.</p> <h3 id="waiting-for-external-change-approval">"waiting for external change approval"<a class="dc-anchor" href="#waiting-for-external-change-approval" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Possible causes</strong> — the change uses <strong>External</strong> approval. It is fail-closed: it runs only once an external approval is recorded on it.</p> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — have the external authority's integration send its verdict to <code>POST /api/v1/change-requests/<id>/external-approval</code>, or record it by hand with <strong>Record external approval</strong> on the <em>External change record</em> card (see <a href="#record-an-external-approval">Record an external approval</a>).</p> <p><strong>Verification</strong> — the <em>External change record</em> card shows <em>external approval on record</em> or <em>manual (approved in SATOM)</em>.</p> <h3 id="email-send-failed-notice-marked-as-sent-configure-settings-email-to-deliver-it-automatically">"Email send failed: …" / "Notice marked as sent. Configure Settings -> Email to deliver it automatically."<a class="dc-anchor" href="#email-send-failed-notice-marked-as-sent-configure-settings-email-to-deliver-it-automatically" title="Permanent link">#</a></h3> <p><strong>Possible causes</strong> — SMTP not configured or refused, or no recipient. <strong>Mark notified</strong> sends to the change's <em>Notify on completion</em> list and, when that is empty, to the default recipients of Settings → Email.</p> <p><strong>Solution</strong> — configure Settings → Email, fill in the change's <em>Notify on completion</em> list (or the e-mail default recipients) and press <strong>Mark notified</strong> again.</p> <h2 id="advanced">Advanced<a class="dc-anchor" href="#advanced" title="Permanent link">#</a></h2> <details class="dc-adv"> <summary><span class="dc-adv-tag">Advanced</span> The run gate</summary> <p>At fire time the scheduler asks the bound change, in order: closed? → refused; not <em>approved / scheduled / in progress</em> → <em>"change request is not approved"</em>; external mode without a recorded external approval → <em>"waiting for external change approval"</em>; no window start → <em>"no maintenance window"</em>; before start → <em>"before the maintenance window"</em>; after end → <em>"after the maintenance window"</em>. Only <em>"inside the maintenance window"</em> runs.</p> <p>The change must also cover the bound row: the same action, and only devices the change names. Otherwise the run is skipped with <em>"change request #N authorizes 'X', not 'Y'"</em>, <em>"change request #N does not cover device id(s) …"</em> or <em>"change request #N authorizes named devices; this action targets the whole fleet"</em>, and the change is left untouched.</p> </details> <details class="dc-adv"> <summary><span class="dc-adv-tag">Advanced</span> Frozen data</summary> <ul> <li><strong>Reference</strong> <code>CR-<year>-<id></code> is stamped at creation and never recalculated.</li> <li><strong>Affected services</strong> come from the cited pre-upgrade runs (merged across all of them) or, without any, from a live read at creation.</li> <li><strong>Change-type wording</strong> is frozen into the change at approval; later edits on Change Types do not alter an approved document.</li> <li>Reserved parameters (<code>change_request_id</code>, <code>target_version</code>) cannot be set from a form; <code>target_version</code> is derived from the declared destination and the cited pre-upgrade runs, which must agree.</li> </ul> </details> <details class="dc-adv"> <summary><span class="dc-adv-tag">Advanced</span> Rollout rounds</summary> <p>A rollout plan (appliances per round, minutes between rounds, default gap 60 minutes, at most 24 rounds, the last round must start before the window ends) can be saved on a draft and becomes real scheduled actions at approval. When the window has already started, all rounds are shifted to begin one minute from now, keeping their spacing. Rounds 2..N are separate one-shot actions named <code>… - round i/N</code>. Plans are saved from the <a href="upgrade-flow.html">Upgrade Flow</a>; the change page's <strong>Schedule</strong> button binds a single round.</p> </details></article> <div class="dc-tags"><a
